summary: Memory hydration is a precondition for governed writes on the Claude Code surface. Repository-write authority comes from Git (dedicated worktree + branch + merge analysis), NOT from memory state: a memory phase-lock neither authorizes, denies, nor serializes ordinary repository mutation. Single front door: the canonical memory control plane (ops/memory, memory-control-plane/v1) via thin hooks; no provider client, no provider URL, no bearer (realignment stage C8). Interactive (model-initiated) durable writes are memory.phase_lock -> memory.write_governed on the package-owned l9-graphite-memory MCP server; that lock is a memory-write consistency precondition only, and generic memory.ingest / the operator CLI write are not the model's alternative to it (ADR-0030 items 7-9, CANONICAL_LAW 8.3). Enforced at PreToolUse. Operator-only breakglass: L9_MEMORY_ENFORCEMENT_BREAKGLASS. No ENFORCEMENT=off side door. A subagent inherits read evidence only: it never closes, never writes, never hydrates under its own identity.

interactive_memory_write.note: Agents MUST be able to write durable memory and MUST NOT write to the provider transport. The model's write is memory.phase_lock then memory.write_governed on the canonical MCP server; MemoryService grants the lock after a conflict check on the namespace snapshot and re-verifies the digest inside the admitting transaction. The lock governs memory-write consistency only: it does not authorize a source edit, serialize git, or replace worktree/branch/publication governance (rules/96 E7/E8/E10). Routing a model-authored fact through generic memory.ingest or the operator CLI write to avoid the lock is a violation; SessionStart/sessionEnd/repair/reconciliation/diagnostics adapters use their purpose-specific ops/memory operations over the same admission path and are not second egresses.

prefetch.note: SessionStart thin wrap of the canonical session hydration (ops.memory.hydration via the session-packet compiler). Writes receipt on success. Fail-open.

gate.note: Emits a PreToolUse permissionDecision. Denies a matched governed write when its required preconditions are unmet.

writeback.note: Stop thin wrap of the canonical close (continuation capsule -> governed candidate -> memory.close). Subagent/background Stop records skipped_subagent and closes nothing. Fail-open.

session_prefetch.satisfied_by: a session receipt under state.session_receipt_glob whose session_id matches the current session and whose age is < state.session_ttl_seconds
session_prefetch.gate_shape: fresh hydration? yes -> continue; no -> hydrate, then continue
session_prefetch.note: The ONLY permitted memory precondition on repository mutation. There is no conflicts -> phase-lock -> edit-permission chain.

governed_writes.description: Edits to governance-authority paths require that memory was hydrated this session. Isolation and collision safety are Git's job (worktree + branch + publication gate).
Any other edit still requires that memory was prefetched this session.
Local history mutation and publication require session hydration only. Push/PR routing is governed by L4 and the publication gate, never by memory lock state.
External GitHub writes require session hydration only; collision safety comes from the publication overlap gate.

operator_override.note: Admin/operator-only key to the back door. Non-empty reason allows governed writes and appends .l9/memory/overrides.jsonl. Agents cannot set this for their own hooks. There is no L9_MEMORY_ENFORCEMENT=off escape hatch and no agent-facing force-lock.

repository_authority.note: Distinct authorities that MUST NOT be substituted for one another; see rules/96-multi-agent-main-bound-execution.mdc.
repository_authority.shared_knowledge: canonical L9 memory (l9-graphite-memory MemoryService; Graphiti only as its projection)
prohibited: memory conflict as a repository-wide mutation lock
branch identity as the memory namespace
